sources.entry: SimpleX Chat - The most private and secure chat and applications platform - now with double ratchet E2E encryption. AGPL-3.0 Haskell

summary.one_liner: SimpleX Chat is an end-to-end encrypted messaging platform and client set (mobile, desktop, terminal) that assigns users no identifiers, built on a client-server relay network.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes SimpleX Chat apps for Android, iOS, and a terminal/CLI client on Linux, macOS, and Windows, plus a desktop client. Messages use double ratchet end-to-end encryption with an additional encryption layer, and the README lists post-quantum key exchange in the ratchet. Users connect via one-time invitation links or QR codes rather than phone numbers or usernames. The SimpleX network uses relay servers that hold messages only until delivery, and clients can use Tor or their own servers. Groups, file sending via the XFTP protocol, voice and video calls, and a bot API (local WebSocket server with the CLI) are also covered. The README includes a feature roadmap and a list of third-party security reviews.
use_cases: private messaging without phone numbers or usernames
running a self-hosted messaging relay server
terminal-based chat from the command line
how_to_run: curl -o- | bash  (install script URL is missing from the README text)
simplex-chat  (run from terminal after installing the CLI client)
notable: No user identifiers of any kind, not even random numbers, so contacts cannot be linked across conversations
Relay servers do not store messages after delivery and do not communicate with each other
Private message routing by default from v6.0 to hide IP addresses from relays
Security reviews by Trail of Bits in 2022 and 2024
Manual queue rotation and optional Tor access to messaging servers
caveats: README states the project is a work in progress and early stage, with possible bugs and missing features
Default servers are provided on a best-effort basis with no SLA
Automatic queue rotation, message mixing, and reproducible client builds are listed as planned, not implemented
